name: Porokeratotic Eccrine Ostial and Dermal Duct Nevus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for PEODDN

criteria.description: Presence of linear, hyperkeratotic papules and plaques following Blaschko lines
Histological identification of cornoid lamellae associated with eccrine ostia and dermal ducts
Congenital or early childhood onset of lesions
Positive staining for eccrine duct markers in affected tissue

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesions plus confirmatory histopathology showing cornoid lamellae involving eccrine ostia and ducts
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; genetic testing is not routinely performed.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Linear hyperkeratotic papules and plaques along Blaschko lines
searchTerms: raised scaly skin lines following skin patterns
linear thickened skin bumps along skin lines
scaly papules arranged in lines on skin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Histopathological presence of cornoid lamellae involving eccrine ostia and ducts
searchTerms: skin biopsy showing cornoid lamellae in sweat ducts
histology with abnormal skin layers in sweat gland openings
microscopic skin changes involving sweat duct structures

common.symptomName: Asymptomatic or mildly pruritic skin lesions
searchTerms: skin bumps with little or no itching
lesions on one side of body

common.symptomName: Lesions present at birth or early infancy
searchTerms: birth or early life skin lesions

occasional.symptomName: Lesion progression or expansion over time

rare.symptomName: Malignant transformation to squamous cell carcinoma
searchTerms: cyst turning into squamous cell carcinoma
nerve or brain abnormalities linked to skin lesion
brain or nerve issues with skin findings

rare.symptomName: Painful lesions due to secondary infection

laboratory: Histopathology showing cornoid lamellae with involvement of eccrine ostia and ducts

distinguishingFeatures: Lesions lack involvement of eccrine ostia and ducts
Histopathology shows cornoid lamellae but not specifically associated with eccrine structures
Absence of cornoid lamellae on histology
Histology shows hyperkeratosis and acanthosis without cornoid lamellae
Lesions not specifically involving eccrine ducts

redFlags: Rapid lesion growth or ulceration suggesting malignant transformation
Secondary bacterial infection with systemic symptoms
Neurological deficits in association with skin lesions
references: Takahashi H, et al. Porokeratotic eccrine ostial and dermal duct nevus: a review of clinical and histopathologic features. J Dermatol. 2018;45(3):293-299.
